audit_findings.title: Dealer-repurchase guarantees create an unmodeled senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: Latest filed commitments $3,719.061m, equal to 11.2x anchor OE; filed reserve $19.268m, or 5.8% of anchor OE; stressed net loss unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A dealer default requires cash repurchases; losses after collateral resale would reduce OE or require a separate equity-value bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s total commercial commitments under standby repurchase obligations on dealer inventory financing as of July 31, 2025 and July 31, 2024 were $ 3,484,235 and $ 3,642,137 , respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The contingent obligation demonstrably exists and has increased from $3,484.235m at July 2025. However, gross commitments are not economic losses: vehicles provide resale recovery, recent settled losses were not material, and the filing identifies no current dealer defaults expected to be material. The record therefore cannot establish that the unmodeled net loss is large enough to change value, although the exposure and dealer concentration make that possible.
audit_findings.action: Obtain dealer-level exposure, aging, lender curtailments, collateral resale discounts, FreedomRoads concentration and default assumptions; reconcile the resulting stressed loss to the $19.268m reserve and rerun the bridge or normalized OE.

audit_findings.title: Equity-method results may be mixed into OE while the investments are added separately
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 equity-method loss $3.775m, 1.1% of $331.7m anchor OE; if entirely retained, base-case sensitivity is $50.2m or $0.96 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method results enter the OE numerator while the separately valued stakes enter the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s share of income and losses accounted for under the equity method of accounting are included in Other income, net in the Consolidated Statements of Income and Comprehensive Income.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the loss was removed remains unresolved, but its maximum identified anchor-year effect is small relative to the $331.7m anchor and the $93.87 base value per share. Because FY2025 contained a loss, retaining it while adding the stake would understate—not overstate—value by approximately $0.96 per share under the supplied base-case capitalization.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $3.775m FY2025 loss and all other equity-method results through OE, remove them consistently, and confirm that the $125.5m bridge addition represents the corresponding net stakes.

audit_findings.title: The forward capital requirement may exceed the amount implicit in anchor OE
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 cash capital expenditure $122.987m; original FY2026 plan $225.000m; latest filing shows $98.136m spent plus approximately $60.000m remaining, implying approximately $158.136m, $35.149m above FY2025; that difference has a base-case sensitivity of $467.2m or $8.94 per share if entirely recurring maintenance
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring maintenance capital reduces OE, while capital supporting modeled growth must be reflected in scenario reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: Our current estimate of committed and internally approved capital spend for fiscal 2026 is $225,000, primarily for certain building projects as well as replacing and upgrading machinery, equipment and other assets throughout our facilities to be used in the ordinary course of business.
audit_findings.explanation: The higher forward spending is demonstrated, but its maintenance-versus-growth composition is not. The latest implied FY2026 total is below the original $225m plan yet still above FY2025. If the $35.149m increase were entirely recurring maintenance omitted from the anchor, the effect would be substantial, but the record does not establish that classification or persistence.
audit_findings.action: Classify FY2026 spending by maintenance, replacement, compliance, restructuring, automation, capacity and growth; then rerun OE and growth reinvestment using only the recurring amounts not already represented.

audit_findings.title: Vendor-term extension may have inflated FY2025 cash conversion
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 total working-capital benefit $65.877m, 19.9% of anchor OE; disclosed vendor-term portion unquantified; the full disclosed benefit has a base-case sensitivity of $875.6m or $16.75 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A temporary accounts-payable increase raises operating cash flow and OE if the anchor uses reported cash conversion; capitalizing it overstates recurring distributable cash.
audit_findings.evidence: The change in net working capital provided additional operating cash of $65,877 during fiscal 2025, primarily due to an increase in accounts payable from extending vendor payment terms on certain raw material purchases, partially offset by required income tax payments exceeding the income tax provisions for fiscal 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that working capital added $65.877m and attributes the benefit primarily to extended vendor terms. Inclusion in OE and the exact vendor-related amount remain unresolved, but the disclosed total is nearly large enough, if temporary and fully capitalized, to eliminate the $16.93-per-share gap between market price and base value. It is therefore reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile anchor OE to the cash-flow statement, isolate the accounts-payable benefit caused by changed terms, determine whether the terms are permanent, reverse any temporary amount, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: A one-time deferred-tax remeasurement may remain in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed nonrecurring tax benefit $15.314m, 4.6% of anchor OE; if fully retained, base-case sensitivity is $203.6m or $3.89 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A noncash, one-time tax benefit can inflate anchor OE; recurring enacted tax rates should instead affect future cash taxes.
audit_findings.evidence: The effect of the foreign tax law change of $ 15,314 noted above is due to revaluing the July 31, 2025 deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities associated with our German operations as a result of Germany passing legislation in July 2025 reducing its corporate income tax rate in the coming years.
audit_findings.explanation: The remeasurement is demonstrably nonrecurring, but whether it entered OE is unresolved. Even assuming the entire $15.314m was retained dollar-for-dollar, the computed effect is approximately $3.89 per share, which is not sufficient by itself to overturn the relationship between the $76.94 market price and the $93.87 base value.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $15.314m benefit through the OE calculation, remove it if present, retain only recurring cash-tax effects from enacted German rates, and document the reconciliation.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain a nonrecurring insurance gain
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed insurance gain $12.153m, 3.7% of anchor OE; if fully retained, base-case sensitivity is $161.5m or $3.09 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A one-time insurance recovery can inflate anchor OE and then be capitalized as recurring operating cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, the Company recognized a total gain of $ 12,153 related to this insurance settlement, which includes $ 5,837 for business interruption and the remainder primarily relates to the insurance replacement reimbursement exceeding the carrying value of the damaged property.
audit_findings.explanation: The $12.153m settlement gain is demonstrably nonrecurring, while its inclusion in OE remains unresolved. Assuming the full gain remained in the anchor, its approximately $3.09-per-share base-case effect is too small by itself to change the valuation conclusion relative to the $76.94 market price and $93.87 base value.
audit_findings.action: Trace both the $5.837m business-interruption component and the property-replacement component through OE and cash-flow classifications; remove any included gain while retaining ordinary insurance costs and genuine uninsured operating losses.
